The REVIEW is structural: introduce one source of truth for the repo roster (e.g. repos.json at the workspace root, or reuse tim's config) that the Makefile, scripts/setup.sh and scripts/update.sh all read, instead of three hand-maintained copies.
findings.why: The roster is hardcoded THREE times and the copies have already drifted: Makefile lists 10 repos, scripts/setup.sh lists 10, scripts/update.sh's fallback lists only 8 (missing trade-imports-address-book and trade-imports-ins-frontend), so `bash scripts/update.sh` with no args silently skips two repos. A generic workspace that may later host a different repo family needs the roster to be data, not three literals. Requires a human ruling on where the single source lives — this is a behaviour change, not a rename.

BREAKAGE: docker compose namespaces containers, the default network and named/anon volumes by project name, so any stack running under the old name is orphaned by this change — its containers keep running, `stop-stack.sh` under the new name will not see them, and mongo/floci volumes are effectively abandoned. Sequence: tear the stack down under the OLD name first (`docker compose -p trade-imports-animals down --volumes --remove-orphans`), then land the rename, then bring it back up.
